scope: Shared token reservations, usage attribution/reporting, API/CLI/settings and schema-5 migration; not full M4 acceptance
checks: Atomic shared reservations cover chat, tool continuations, index/query embeddings and both reranking paths. Cached vectors do not trigger new model calls.

Actual input/output/cache totals settle calls. Cached input is included in input; interrupted, unknown or malformed usage retains a conservative charge. Streaming uses additive SDK usage and settles actual totals only after complete delivery.

UTC daily and per-credential rolling-hour caps are shared. Unknown reservations survive restart; deleting a conversation preserves charges. Retained pre-ledger chat usage is included without double-counting new rows.

Interactive spending revalidates authority. Admitted ingestion keeps its initiating credential, generation and account epoch; derived calendar-member embedding jobs inherit the container import attribution while retaining their own job id.

Administrator usage reports expose bounded interval and group counts with explicit truncation. The API, CLI and Settings share the same report. Numeric daily-budget edits reload and zero budget leaves keyword search available.

Schema version 5 adds the ledger correlation table and indexes. Initialized schema upgrades require complete encrypted backups; an earlier M4 state upgrades in a dedicated regression test. Portable export explicitly includes the added table.
Reviewed composition and OpenAPI updates add one usage service, two usage routes and report schemas.
limitations: Classification, enrichment/batch/frontmatter write-back and remaining provider integrations are not completed by this checkpoint. Future inference consumers must use the shared ledger.
Dollar cost calculation is not implemented; reports cover tokens and attribution.

The real transcript contains no pricing vocabulary. The local-model qualification checks a real speaker/topic question and current timestamped citation metadata, without a separate human semantic review.
Hardened deployment, sustained-write daemon restore, external mount-point restore, large-corpus resource gates and release operations remain open.
